hook.text: What if concrete could fix its own cracks — like skin healing a cut?

buildup.text: Bacteria embedded in concrete capsules activate when cracks let water in.

discovery.text: The bacteria produce limestone — calcium carbonate — that seals the crack naturally.

twist.text: The bacteria survive dormant for 200+ years inside the concrete — waiting for a crack.

climax.text: Dutch researcher Henk Jonkers pioneered bio-concrete — now in pilot projects worldwide.

punchline.text: Living concrete that heals itself. Biology inside engineering.

quiz.question: How do bacteria heal cracks in self-healing concrete?
options: They consume the cracked concrete and form new cement paste
They produce calcium carbonate (limestone) that fills and seals the crack
They generate heat that melts the crack edges back together
